title: Modal verbs: obligation and deduction
intro: Modal verbs for rules, permission, advice (B1) and for guessing what is true now or what happened in the past (B2).

sections.title: Modals of permission and obligation
sections.summary: Use modal verbs to say what is allowed, necessary or forbidden.

tables.caption: Obligation and permission
head: meaning
modal verb
example
rows: You must wear a seat belt.
don't have to / needn't / don't need to

uses: Must is from the speaker (a personal feeling). Have to is from outside (a rule): I must call my mum. We have to wear a uniform.
Mustn't and don't have to are very different: mustn't = forbidden, don't have to = not necessary.
In the past use had to for obligation and was / were allowed to for permission. Must has no past.
Needn't + base form is possible in British English.

examples.text: You don't have to come, but you can.
Students are not allowed to use phones.

mistakes.wrong: You mustn't come if you don't want to.
mistakes.right: You don't have to come if you don't want to.
mistakes.why: No obligation, so use don't have to.

checks.question: Choose: You (mustn't / don't have to) enter. It is dangerous.
Choose: You (mustn't / don't have to) bring food. We have lots.

sections.title: Modals of deduction
sections.summary: Use modal verbs to say how sure you are about the present or the past.
uses: Present: He must be at work. His car is outside.
Past: She must have left early. Her desk is empty.
Possibility: It might rain later. They may have missed the train.
The opposite of must in a deduction is can't, not mustn't.
Use the continuous when the action is in progress: He must be sleeping.

examples.text: That can't be Jo. She is in Spain.
They must have forgotten the time.
He might have lost his key.

mistakes.wrong: She mustn't be at home. The lights are off.
mistakes.right: She can't be at home. The lights are off.

checks.question: Complete: The shop is dark. It ___ (must / can't) be open.
checks.explanation: Sure that it is not open.

checks.question: Complete: I can't find my glasses. I ___ (must / mustn't) have left them at work.
